summary: Cross-border egress and session-sticky routing causing sporadic latency spikes — clarification & mitigation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer FinOptima reports intermittent 200–800ms additional tail latency on requests from eu-west that should be served by their dedicated eu pool. They observe spikes approximately 1–3 times per 1k requests and see traces indicating a short-lived cross-region egress to us-east for some requests despite region affinity.

Impact:
- Sporadic increased tail latency (affects user-facing search/assist features).
- No obvious 5xxs; throughput unaffected.
- Customer worried about data egress policy compliance and cost implications of cross-region routing.

Environment:
- Customer tier: dedicated reserved capacity
- Primary region: eu-west (eu-west-1)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a steady stream of generation requests pinned to model redwood/open-llama-7b against customer's dedicated eu endpoint (500 rps, typical prompt length ~120 tokens).
2) Monitor per-request region tag in trace and routing logs for a 24h window.
3) Correlate latency spikes to any route changes or capacity events in the serving logs.
observed_behavior: Small subset (~0.1%-0.3%) of requests were routed out of eu-west to us-east briefly and returned results; traces show an extra ~200-800ms attributable to cross-region network hop and additional TLS handshakes. No model fallback to smaller-quantized variants observed in the traces.
expected_behavior: All requests from customer's eu-resident endpoint should be served from the dedicated eu-west pool (no cross-region egress) unless explicit failover or capacity policy is triggered.
logs_and_traces: Trace snippet: trace_id=abcd1234: route_decision=geo_affinity->eu-west; transient_routing_override=us-east; tcp_rtt_delta=120ms; tls_handshake=85ms
API logs: 200 responses; no upstream 5xx; service.agent=dedicated-eu-v2
investigation_notes: Customer provided sample traces and timestamps (2026-03-09 14:02:10Z to 14:30:00Z).
Checked routing policy config for customer: geo_affinity=preferred, allow_cross_region_failover=true, failover_threshold=85th_percentile_latency>500ms
Dedicated pool metrics show a short spike in kernel queue wait on eu-west GPU node group at 2026-03-09 14:15Z coincident with reported spikes.
No autoscaler events that fully drained pool; there was a transient pod OOM on node eu-w-3 which triggered a short-lived request re-route to shared capacity in us-east.
Billing meter shows negligible cross-region bytes but customer accounting concerns remain.
comments: Customer (FinOptima) - 2026-03-10: We're seeing occasional latency spikes and some internal compliance flags for cross-border calls. Can you confirm whether 'preferred' geo-affinity can be made strict to fully prevent any egress out of region?

Support (Asha Mehta) - 2026-03-10: Thanks for the report — I've escalated to infra and collected traces. Asking SRE to check for transient node-level issues in eu-west and to confirm routing behavior logic.

SRE (Evan Park) - 2026-03-11: Preliminary find: a single dedicated worker experienced an OOM and requests in-flight were diverted to fallback routing which currently prefers lowest-latency available capacity (which can be cross-region). Investigating whether we can short-circuit to strict-local policy for customer pools with 'no-egress' compliance needs.

Support (Priya Nair) - 2026-03-11: Workaround proposed to customer: enable 'strict_local_failover=false' -> (note: docs call this geo_affinity.mode with options preferred|strict) — set to strict to prevent cross-region fallback; recommend applying alongside autoscaler tuning to avoid OOM-driven diversions. Guidance sent with steps to apply via Console and API.

Customer (FinOptima) - 2026-03-11: We need a documented SLA for 'no-egress' behavior and confirmation that enabling strict mode won't increase request failures during local capacity pressure. Also want recommended autoscaler settings for steady 500rps workload.

SRE (Evan Park) - 2026-03-12: Follow-up: enabling strict geo-affinity will prevent cross-region reroutes but may surface 429/503 during local capacity exhaustion; recommended pattern: (1) strict geo-affinity with (2) increased reserved capacity or configured burst pools in-region and (3) reduce pod memory headroom to avoid OOMs, plus pre-warming. Drafted infra-runbook changes for 'strict-local' customers.
resolution: Pending - workaround documented and delivered to customer. Action items: (1) advise customer to switch geo_affinity.mode to strict if they accept risk of local failures, (2) SRE to publish runbook updates and autoscaler tuning recommendations, (3) infra to add a safety metric to detect node OOM patterns and trigger preemptive routing alerts.
next_steps: 1) Support to confirm with customer whether they want strict geo-affinity applied (ticket owner: Priya Nair).
2) SRE to convert runbook notes into a Confluence page and link the PR (owner: Evan Park).
3) Infra to propose an autoscaler memory headroom baseline for dedicated pools (owner: Platform Eng lead).
